A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Matérn-kernel reconstruction work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShapeNet and SRB reconstruction experiments, learned-kernel comparisons, noise tests, generalization results and convergence analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds texture-reconstruction results on GSO and Objaverse and a positional-consistency demonstration.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix H add a limited extension from scalar signed-distance prediction to four outputs: signed distance and RGB. It concatenates color targets into the existing KRR solve and interpolates colors onto extracted surfaces. The underlying kernels, geometric reconstruction procedure and learned NKF framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 extends coverage beyond geometry reconstruction to texture reconstruction, with quantitative evaluation on ten GSO objects and qualitative examples from Objaverse. Appendix A also adds a scene containing two identical chairs at different positions. Existing ShapeNet and SRB coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The SRB accuracy comparisons add SAP, DiGS, VisCo and OG-INR in v2 Tables 1 and 6. FFN and SIREN remain accuracy comparators but disappear from the SRB runtime comparison when it becomes Table 2. The ShapeNet comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added texture experiment introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: 10,000 versus 2,500 sampled points, PSNR and LPIPS, and texture-atlas evaluation on the original mesh and UV coordinates to control for differences in reconstructed geometry. Appendix H specifies ten GSO objects. The retained geometry experiments preserve their splits, sampling settings, metrics and solvers.

E4.justification: New Appendix A and Figure 8 test positional consistency using two identical chairs within one scene, contrasting arc-cosine and Matérn reconstructions. The existing bandwidth, noise, category-generalization and convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds SRB scores for four comparators and new texture and positional-consistency results; retained geometry accuracy values are unchanged. New Table 3 reports Matérn versus arc-cosine PSNR of 19.61 versus 19.34 at 10,000 points and 18.92 versus 18.88 at 2,500 points. Sparse LPIPS instead favors arc-cosine, 2.09 versus 2.15. The FFN and SIREN runtimes of 337.91 and 599.00 seconds in v1 are removed.

T1.justification: The reconstruction-error bound, optimal-bandwidth derivation and principal proofs already appear in v1 and are retained. v2 adds a centered arc-cosine definition and translation-invariance argument in Appendix A, plus Remark 7 extending the SIREN correspondence to stationary kernels generally. It omits the general half-integer Matérn expansion and explicit taper-kernel formula.

C1.justification: The main claims about tunable Matérn reconstruction, computational efficiency and learned kernels persist. The introduction adds superiority for high-frequency texture reconstruction and explicitly claims more than fourfold faster training than NKF. The introduction and conclusion also elevate the existing reconstruction-error bound and bandwidth guidance into an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains stationarity through centering requirements and consistency between repeated objects, qualifies v1's compact-support assertion as exponential decay and effective compactness, and recommends h = 1 as a starting point. It also interprets sharper textures as evidence against spectral bias, although its blanket texture-superiority language overlooks the sparse LPIPS reversal.

D1.justification: Appendix H documents duplicated RGB targets, the multi-output solve, mesh/color extraction, texture-atlas construction, ten named GSO assets and their access location. v2 also discloses SRB inputs of up to 100,000 points, while dropping the explicit KeOps implementation reference. Existing reconstruction settings and the project-code link remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the four new SRB comparators, GSO, Objaverse and texture-atlas evaluation, while removing Charlier et al. (2021) and Peng et al. (2020). The core related-work narrative remains. Section 3.3 broadens the novelty statement from a Matérn/neural-network correspondence to a connection between SIRENs and kernel methods generally.

P1.justification: v2 merges the former background and theoretical-analysis sections into Section 3, adds contribution bullets, rewrites selected explanations and the conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices. These are localized structural and language refinements within the retained overall narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds texture and positional-consistency figures and a texture-results table, expands SRB comparison tables, and separates runtime reporting. Several qualitative figures reorder method columns and add input-point or ground-truth panels. The existing RKHS-norm inset becomes numbered Figure 5. These changes substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and assessability through the compact-support correction, input/ground-truth panels, broader SRB comparisons and an explicitly geometry-controlled texture protocol. The gains are limited: the main geometry results and proofs are retained, texture evaluation covers only ten GSO objects, and the superiority claim overlooks worse sparse LPIPS in Table 3. Removing FFN/SIREN timing evidence also narrows the runtime comparison.
